text:
alice: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a ‘token stability window’ for pagination/resume tokens. Idea: server guarantees a resume token stays valid for a short window (e.g. N seconds) after issuance so client retries/short reconnects can resume without restarting the whole scan. Wanted feedback on tradeoffs and how SDKs (py/ts/go) should surface/automate this.

ben: high-level Q — what exactly are we guaranteeing? is it a passive TTL or do we need server-side state pinned for the token that could blow memory on large scans?

alice: good call. two model options: passive token (stateless opaque cursor that encodes position + expiry) vs pinned server-side checkpoint (small state keyed by token). passives scale, pinning gives more flexible semantics (renew, invalidate early).

carla: we should probably design for passive-first (encode sufficient position info) and optionally support pinned tokens for heavy/resumable jobs. also return expires_at in response so clients know.

dave: SDK ergonomics question — should SDKs auto-retry across expired tokens? e.g. if a retry wakes up 10s after expiry, do we surface an error or try to re-run from start? Different languages will have different expectations.

erin: I'd vote for predictable defaults: SDKs should not automatically restart the whole scan unless user opts in. Better: fail with a specialized error (CursorExpired) so app can decide. Provide a convenience pattern to restart+dedupe.

ben: +1. Also recommend returning a server hint like recommended_retry_window in the API response so clients can apply shorter retry budgets. Example: 
```
GET /v1/items?page_size=100&cursor=abc123
200 { items: [...], next_cursor: "def456", cursor_expires_at: 1722224000, recommended_retry_window: 30 }
```

carla: SDK surface options: 1) high-level API keeps cursor as string and throws CursorExpired error 2) low-level Cursor object that exposes expiry, refresh() and metadata. Expose refresh but don't auto-call in browser TS by default because refresh may require extra auth/cors hops.

alice: cross-lang specifics:
- Python: provide both sync and async Cursor helper with an opt-in auto_refresh=True flag.
- Go: small Cursor struct with Refresh(ctx) method and explicit semantics.
- TypeScript: in Node SDK mirror Go behavior, in browser keep lighter surface and no auto-refresh.

dave: retry semantics: recommend exponential backoff with jitter but respect recommended_retry_window. Default max attempts=4 and cap total retry time to the recommended window if present. Expose RetryPolicy config in SDK constructors.

erin: failure modes to consider: leader failover might invalidate pinned tokens early -> server should surface an explicit InvalidatedCursor error with optional final_position so clients can resume from nearest checkpoint.

ben: tests we need: interop matrix for py/ts/go verifying same CursorExpired/InvalidatedCursor behaviors, stress test that simulates failover and token revocation, and a network jitter test to validate default retry budget.

carla: telemetry: emit events 'cursor_issued', 'cursor_refresh', 'cursor_retry_exceeded', 'cursor_invalidated' with simple labels so Optimize/Console can surface regression alerts.

alice: concrete proposal to capture: 
1) Server returns cursor_expires_at (epoch) and optional recommended_retry_window (int seconds).
2) Default server-recommended window = 30s; will vary by deployment (Dedicated vs Hosted).
3) SDK defaults: exponential backoff w/ jitter, max_attempts=4, but will cap retries to recommended_retry_window when provided.
4) Python/Go: ship a Cursor helper with explicit Refresh() and optional auto_refresh config. TS: low-level refresh API; Node auto_refresh opt-in, browser opt-out by default.
5) On server invalidation produce deterministic InvalidatedCursor error + optional final_position to allow graceful fallback.

dave: LGTM. we should also document failure semantics clearly in the SDK READMEs and provide a tiny example snippet for each language.

carla: small API nit: add a short header `X-Cursor-Stability: <seconds>` in responses so intermediate proxies can be aware. Might help routing and caching.

erin: follow-ups: add RFC section for telemetry fields, update SDK README templates, write interop tests, and pick default window per environment. I can own the test matrix.

alice: thanks — i'll draft the RFC with these decisions and link to a spike branch for the Cursor helper. Proposed default window=30s for hosted; Dedicated will expose config. Will add examples for py/ts/go.

carla: :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: merged spike/token-stability to staging (CI passed)
